335067.title: The uniqueness conjecture for universal perfect state transfer among circulants with property $\mathbb{T}$
335067.literal_statement: A complex unit gain graph is a graph whose adjacency matrix has complex entries, with each nonzero entry of unit magnitude. A graph has **property $\mathbb{T}$** if all nonzero coefficients in its adjacency matrix are complex numbers with unit magnitude. The notation $\operatorname{Circ}(0,-\mathtt{i},\mathtt{i})$ denotes the circulant graph specified by the first row $(0,-\mathtt{i},\mathtt{i})$. **Uniqueness conjecture.** $\operatorname{Circ}(0,-\mathtt{i},\mathtt{i})$ is the only circulant with property $\mathbb{T}$ which has universal perfect state transfer. This conjecture proposes a complete classification of circulant graphs with property $\mathbb{T}$ exhibiting universal perfect state transfer; the preceding discussion establishes uniqueness among graphs on three vertices, while the general case remains open.

335297.title: Kiss–Rozgonyi–Sándor conjecture on higher-order representation functions
335297.literal_statement:
Let $h>2$, and let $C$ and $D$ be different infinite sets of nonnegative integers. For a set $A$, write $A(z)=\sum_{a\in A}z^a$, and let $F_C(z)$, $F_D(z)$, and $T(z)$ denote the generating polynomials of the finite sets $F_C$, $F_D$, and $T$, respectively. The functions $R_{h,C}^{(1)}$ and $R_{h,D}^{(1)}$ count ordered representations as sums of $h$ elements of the indicated set.

**Kiss–Rozgonyi–Sándor conjecture.** The equality $R_{h,C}^{(1)}(n)=R_{h,D}^{(1)}(n)$ from some point onward holds if and only if there exist positive integers $n_0$ and $M$, and finite sets $F_C,F_D,T$ satisfying $F_C\cup F_D\subset[0,Mn_0-1]$ and $T\subset[0,M-1]$, such that

$$
C=F_C\cup\{lM+t:l\ge n_0,\,t\in T\},
$$

$$
D=F_D\cup\{lM+t:l\ge n_0,\,t\in T\},
$$

$$
(1-z^M)^{h-1}\mid(F_C(z)-F_D(z))T(z)^{h-1}.
$$

This conjectures a periodic-tail characterization of pairs of infinite sets whose ordered $h$-fold representation functions eventually coincide, generalizing Nathanson's result for $h=2$.

335684.title: The conjecture on the uniform rigged configuration bijection
335684.literal_statement:
Let $B$ be a tensor product of Kirillov--Reshetikhin crystals of affine type. Let $\operatorname{RC}(B)$ be the corresponding set of rigged configurations, let $\eta$ interchange riggings and coriggings, let $D$ be the energy statistic on $B$, and let $R:B\to B'$ be the combinatorial $R$-matrix for a reordering $B'$ of the tensor factors. The recursively defined map $\widetilde{\Phi}:\operatorname{RC}(B)\to B$ is obtained from the maps $\widetilde{\delta}$, $\operatorname{lb}$, and $\operatorname{ls}$. **Uniform bijection conjecture.** The map $\widetilde{\Phi}$ is a classical crystal isomorphism satisfying

$$
D\circ\widetilde{\Phi}\circ\eta=\operatorname{cc},
$$

and the diagram expressing compatibility with $R$ commutes:

$$
\begin{CD}
\operatorname{RC}(B) @>{\widetilde{\Phi}}>> B\\
@V{\operatorname{id}}VV @VV{R}V\\
\operatorname{RC}(B') @>{\widetilde{\Phi}}>> B'.
\end{CD}
$$
 This consolidates conjectures about the rigged configuration bijection, its statistics, and its compatibility with factor reordering; the paper proves the assertion in a substantial range of affine types, while the stated general form remains open.

336161.title: The automaticity conjecture for generalised-polynomial sequences
336161.literal_statement: Let $f\colon\mathbb{N}_0\to\Omega$ be a sequence, where $\Omega$ is a finite alphabet. Call $f$ **automatic** if it is generated by a finite automaton, and call it a **generalised-polynomial sequence** if its values are given by a generalised polynomial. A sequence is **ultimately periodic** if it agrees with a periodic sequence outside a finite set. **Automaticity conjecture.** If a sequence $f$ is simultaneously automatic and generalised polynomial, then $f$ is ultimately periodic. This is the sequence formulation of the paper's motivating conjecture. The authors note that the Fibonacci word supplies a nontrivial generalised-polynomial sequence for a Zeckendorf-type notion of automaticity, while the conjecture concerns the usual positional notion; partial results are proved, but the general statement remains open.

336237.title: The compositional shuffle conjecture
336237.literal_statement:
Let $X=\{x_1,x_2,\ldots\}$ be an infinite set of variables, and write $x_w=x_{w_1}\cdots x_{w_n}$. Let $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_k)$ be a composition of $n$. For a Dyck path $\pi$ of semilength $n$, let $\operatorname{touch}(\pi)=\alpha$ mean that the successive gaps between its contacts with the main diagonal have lengths $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_k$. Let $\mathcal{WP}_\pi$ be the associated word parking functions, and let $\operatorname{area}(\pi)$ and $\operatorname{dinv}(\pi,w)$ be their statistics. The operator $C_\alpha$ is the compositional creation operator, and $C_\alpha(1)$ denotes its value at $1$.

**The compositional shuffle conjecture.** For any composition $\alpha$,

$$
(-1)^n\nabla C_\alpha(1)=\sum_{\operatorname{touch}(\pi)=\alpha}t^{\operatorname{area}(\pi)}\sum_{w\in\mathcal{WP}_\pi}q^{\operatorname{dinv}(\pi,w)}x_w.
$$

This refines the original shuffle conjecture by partitioning the Dyck-path sum according to the touch composition. It was proved in the Carlsson–Mellit work underlying these lecture notes, so the conjecture is solved.

338762.title: The two-thirds excess conjecture for hypergraph $r$-cuts
338762.literal_statement:
Let $H$ be a $k$-graph with $m$ edges. For fixed parameters satisfying $2\le k\le r$, with $k>3$ or $r>2$, let an $r$-cut be a partition of the vertex set into $r$ parts, and let its size be the number of edges having a vertex in every part. Let $S(k,r)$ denote the Stirling number of the second kind.

**Two-thirds excess conjecture.** Every $k$-graph has an $r$-cut of size

$$
\frac{S(k,r)r!}{r^k}m+\Omega\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(m^{2/3}\aftergroup\egroup\originalright).
$$

The paper proves a lower bound with exponent $5/9$ and constructs examples with excess $O\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(m^{2/3}\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)$, so this conjecture would close the gap between the two bounds. The parameter range and quantifiers are reproduced as stated in the source.

338850.title: Polyhedrality conjecture for linkage matching fields
338850.literal_statement:
Let a **left linkage matching field** be a linkage matching field with the left-side convention, and let it satisfy the **compatible right submatching property** when the following holds. Let $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_r$ be submatchings of matchings in the field on $J\sqcup I_1,\ldots,J\sqcup I_r$, where

$$
I:=\bigcup_{s\in [r]} I_s\subseteq R,
$$

with $|J|+1=|I|$. Then

$$
T=\bigcup_{s\in [r]}\mu_s
$$

is a forest on $J\sqcup I$, and each matching $\mu$ of size $|J|$ in $T$ is compatible with the matchings in the field.

**Polyhedrality conjecture.** A left linkage matching field is polyhedral if and only if it satisfies the compatible right submatching property.

This conjecture characterizes the linkage matching fields arising from matching ensembles, or equivalently the polyhedral ones, through an intrinsic compatibility condition on right submatchings. The source gives no resolution or status evidence beyond presenting it as a conjecture.

339034.title: Kuca's regularity classification conjecture for Ulam and modified Ulam sequences
339034.literal_statement: Let $a<b$ be relatively prime positive integers. Let $\mathcal{U}(a,b)$ denote the Ulam sequence generated by $a,b$, let $\mathcal{V}(a,b)$ denote the corresponding modified Ulam sequence, and call either sequence **regular** when it is eventually a finite union of arithmetic progressions. **Kuca's regularity classification conjecture.** Each of the two sequences is regular if and only if it has finitely many even terms: $\mathcal{U}(a,b)$ is regular if and only if $\mathcal{U}(a,b)$ has finitely many even terms, and $\mathcal{V}(a,b)$ is regular if and only if $\mathcal{V}(a,b)$ has finitely many even terms. Finch's theorem establishes the implication from finitely many even terms to regularity for $\mathcal{V}$-sequences; the converse, and the corresponding full assertion for Ulam sequences, are presented as open.

339403.title: NP-completeness conjecture for the strong geodetic set problem on complete multipartite graphs
339403.literal_statement:
A **strong geodetic set** of a graph is a vertex set satisfying the strong geodetic property, and the associated decision problem asks whether a graph has such a set of size at most a prescribed bound. A complete multipartite graph is a graph whose vertex set is partitioned into independent parts with every pair of vertices in distinct parts adjacent.

**Strong geodetic set complexity conjecture.** The strong geodetic set problem restricted to complete multipartite graphs is NP-complete.

The conjecture is motivated by an analogy with the NP-complete Knapsack problem: selecting parts corresponds approximately to selecting items, with part size acting as weight and the number of pairs within a part as value. The source reports no reduction proving NP-hardness, so the conjecture remains open.

339503.title: Surface-inversion correspondence for spherical parking functions and birooted trees
339503.literal_statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer. A spherical parking function of length $n$ has a degree, and a birooted tree on vertex set $[n]$ has a number of surface inversions, where a surface inversion is a pair of non-root vertices $(\alpha,\beta)$ such that $\beta$ is a descendant of $\alpha$ and $\alpha>\beta$. **Surface-inversion correspondence.** The number of spherical parking functions of length $n$ of degree 
$$
{n \choose 2}-k+1
$$
 is equal to the number of birooted trees on vertex set $[n]$ with $k$ surface inversions. This conjectural correspondence would connect the degree enumeration of spherical parking functions with an inversion statistic on birooted trees, analogous to the classical relationship between parking functions and spanning trees; the supplied text does not indicate whether it has been proved or remains open.

339831.title: The Generalized Delta conjecture
339831.literal_statement:
Let $D$ be a partially labelled decorated Dyck path of size $n+m$ with $m$ zero labels, $n$ nonzero labels, and $k$ decorated rises. Its area word is $a(D)=a_1(D)\cdots a_{n+m}(D)$, where $a_i(D)$ counts the whole squares in the $i$-th row between the path and the main diagonal. The area and dinv statistics are

$$
\mathsf{area}(D)=\sum_{i\notin\mathsf{DRise}(D)}a_i(D),
$$

where decorated rises are excluded from the area, and $\mathsf{dinv}(D)$ counts primary and secondary inversions of the labelled area word. Write $\mathsf{PLD}(m,n)^{\ast k}$ for the set of such paths. **Generalized Delta conjecture.**

$$
\Delta_{h_m}\Delta'_{e_{n-k-1}}e_n=\sum_{D\in\mathsf{PLD}(m,n)^{\ast k}}q^{\mathsf{dinv}(D)}t^{\mathsf{area}(D)}x^D.
$$

This is a generalized form of the Delta conjecture, relating symmetric-function operators to weighted decorated Dyck paths. The source attributes it to Haglund, Remmel, and Wilson; its resolution status is not specified here.
339831.gap: Need full symmetric-function identity for all admissible m,n,k; no decorated-path bijection/operator recursion supplied. Flagship parked.

340526.title: Odd-part partition excess conjecture by residue class
340526.literal_statement:
Let $\operatorname{part}(n,S_{\mathrm{odd}})$ be the set of partitions of $n$ into odd parts, and let $l$ denote the number of parts. **Odd-part excess conjecture.** For each residue class of $n$ modulo $4$, the corresponding excess is positive:

- If $n\equiv 0\pmod 4$, then
 
$$
|\{\lambda\in\operatorname{part}(n,S_{\mathrm{odd}}):l\equiv 0\pmod 4\}|-|\{\lambda\in\operatorname{part}(n,S_{\mathrm{odd}}):l\equiv 2\pmod 4\}|>0.
$$

- If $n\equiv 1\pmod 4$, then
 
$$
|\{\lambda\in\operatorname{part}(n,S_{\mathrm{odd}}):l\equiv 1\pmod 4\}|-|\{\lambda\in\operatorname{part}(n,S_{\mathrm{odd}}):l\equiv 3\pmod 4\}|>0.
$$

- If $n\equiv 2\pmod 4$, then
 
$$
|\{\lambda\in\operatorname{part}(n,S_{\mathrm{odd}}):l\equiv 2\pmod 4\}|-|\{\lambda\in\operatorname{part}(n,S_{\mathrm{odd}}):l\equiv 0\pmod 4\}|>0.
$$

- If $n\equiv 3\pmod 4$, then
 
$$
|\{\lambda\in\operatorname{part}(n,S_{\mathrm{odd}}):l\equiv 3\pmod 4\}|-|\{\lambda\in\operatorname{part}(n,S_{\mathrm{odd}}):l\equiv 1\pmod 4\}|>0.
$$

The conjecture concerns a residue-class refinement of the enumeration of odd-part partitions; the source does not provide a resolution.

340572.title: Möbius function and homotopy type conjecture for weak order on monotone triangles
340572.literal_statement:
Let $T'$ and $T$ be monotone triangles with $T'\leq_W T$, and let $\Delta(T',T)$ denote the order complex of their open interval in $<_W$. Write $\operatorname{Des}(T)$ for the descent set of $T$, let $w_0(J)$ be the longest element associated with $J\subset\operatorname{Des}(T)$, and define

$$
J:=\{m:T'_m\neq T_m\}.
$$

**Homotopy-type conjecture.** The complex $\Delta(T',T)$ is contractible unless

$$
T'=T\times\pi_{w_0(J)},
$$

in which case $\Delta(T',T)$ is homotopy equivalent to a $(\#J-2)$-dimensional sphere.

This conjecture would give a simple description of the homotopy types, and hence the Möbius function, of open intervals in the weak order on monotone triangles, paralleling the corresponding description for weak order on permutations. The supplied text does not indicate whether the claim has been proved or remains open.

340644.title: Early's winding-number formula for the Ehrhart h*-vector of the hypersimplex
340644.literal_statement:
A decorated ordered set partition consists of an ordered partition of $[n]$ whose blocks are decorated by positive integers; it is **hypersimplicial** of type $(k,n)$ when each block $L_i$ with decoration $l_i$ satisfies $1\leq l_i\leq |L_i|-1$. The **winding number** is the integer $d$ determined by the total clockwise path length, namely

$$
w_1+\cdots+w_n=kd,
$$

where $w_i$ is the clockwise distance from the block containing $i$ to the block containing $(i+1)$, with indices taken modulo $n$.

**Early's conjecture.** The number of hypersimplicial decorated ordered set partitions of type $(k,n)$ with winding number $d$ is $h^{*}_d(\Delta_{k,n})$.

This gives a combinatorial interpretation of the Ehrhart $h^{*}$-vector of the hypersimplex $\Delta_{k,n}$. The supplied source does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.

341052.title: Approximation-ratio conjecture for randomized binary sequence design
341052.literal_statement:
Let $\tilde{\boldsymbol{s}}$ be a binary sequence obtained by randomized projection and binary quantization from $\widehat{\boldsymbol{S}}$, where $\widehat{\boldsymbol{S}}$ is the solution to the semidefinite relaxation. Suppose that $\tilde{\boldsymbol{s}}$ satisfies the inequality constraint

$$
\|\mathcal{F}_I\tilde{\boldsymbol{s}}\|_2^2\leq\alpha.
$$

Define the approximation ratio by

$$
\gamma=\frac{\|\mathcal{F}_M\tilde{\boldsymbol{s}}\|_2^2}{\operatorname{Trace}\left(\mathcal{F}_M^H\mathcal{F}_M\widehat{\mathbf{S}}\right)}.
$$

**Approximation-ratio conjecture.** The ratio satisfies

$$
\gamma\geq\frac{\pi}{2}-1.
$$

This conjecture is motivated by analogous approximation guarantees for other quadratically constrained quadratic programs and is asserted for feasible randomized projections. The authors report that a theoretical proof is elusive and validate the claim numerically.

341217.title: Quantized non-negative reduced partition function conjecture
341217.literal_statement:
Let $G=G(a,b,c)$ and let $Z_{{\rm red}}^{G(a,b,c)}(\mathbf{t},q^{1/2})$ denote the $q$-deformed reduced plane partition function. For $\mathbf{d}=(d_0,\ldots,d_{r-1})\in\mathbb N^r$, write $(\mathbf{d},\mathbf{d})$ for the bilinear form appearing in the paper and $\mathbf{t}^{\mathbf{d}}=\prod_i t_i^{d_i}$. **Quantized reduced-partition conjecture.** The function can be written

$$
Z_{{\rm red}}^{G(a,b,c)}(\mathbf{t},q^{1/2})=\sum_{\mathbf{d}\in\mathbb N^r}h_{\mathbf{d}}(q)(-q^{1/2})^{d_0+(\mathbf{d},\mathbf{d})}\mathbf{t}^{\mathbf{d}},
$$

where $h_{\mathbf{d}}(q)\in\mathbb N[q^{\pm1}]$.

This is presented as a quantized version of the preceding reduced-series conjecture. It predicts Laurent-polynomial positivity of the coefficients after extracting the prescribed sign and $q$-power; the paper excerpt gives no resolution.

341357.title: Generalized 2413-balloon Möbius function conjecture
341357.literal_statement:
Let $\beta$ be a permutation, let $i,j$ be indexes, and let $2413 \circledcirc_{i,j} \beta$ denote the permutation formed by inserting $\beta$ into $2413$ between its $i$-th and $i+1$-th columns and between its $j$-th and $j+1$-th rows. Write $\tau \oplus 1$ and $\tau \ominus 1$ for the direct and skew sums with the singleton permutation $1$, and similarly $1 \ominus \tau$ and $1 \oplus \tau$. Let $\mu[\pi]$ denote the Möbius function of the permutation pattern poset. **Generalized 2413-balloon conjecture.** If $(i,j) \in \{(0,1),(0,2),(1,1),(1,2)\}$ and $\pi=2413 \circledcirc_{i,j} \beta$, then

$$
\mu[\pi]=\begin{cases}
0 & \text{if }(i,j)=(0,1)\text{ and }\beta=\tau\oplus 1,\\
0 & \text{if }(i,j)=(0,2)\text{ and }\beta=\tau\ominus 1,\\
0 & \text{if }(i,j)=(1,1)\text{ and }\beta=1\ominus\tau\text{ or }12,\\
0 & \text{if }(i,j)=(1,2)\text{ and }\beta=1\oplus\tau,\\
\mu[\beta] & \text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
$$

The conjecture extends the known cases of generalized 2413-balloons with indexes $(0,0)$ and $(2,2)$; the displayed formula remains unproved in the source.

357690.title: Conjectured quartic-invariant inequalities for the distinct partition function
357690.literal_statement:
Let $q(n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ into distinct parts, and set $a_n=q(n)$. For a quartic binary form, define

$$
A(a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4)=a_0a_4-4a_1a_3+3a_2^2,
$$

$$
B(a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4)=-a_0a_2a_4+a_2^3+a_0a_3^2+a_1^2a_4-2a_1a_2a_3,
$$

$$
I(a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4)=A(a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4)^3-27B(a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4)^2.
$$

**The quartic-invariant conjecture for $q(n)$.** The following inequalities hold:

$$
A(a_{n-1},a_n,a_{n+1},a_{n+2},a_{n+3})>0\quad\text{for }n\geq230,
$$

$$
B(a_{n-1},a_n,a_{n+1},a_{n+2},a_{n+3})>0\quad\text{for }n\geq272,
$$

and

$$
I(a_{n-1},a_n,a_{n+1},a_{n+2},a_{n+3})>0\quad\text{for }n\geq267.
$$

These are proposed as analogues for the distinct partition function of quartic-binary-form invariant inequalities previously studied for the ordinary partition function. The supplied text gives no resolution of these conjectures.
